solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 12 finished cycling within a month

definitions.note: twelve o'clock in the day, a number standing for the time

indicators.note: the rotated piece is placed inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: the word's letters are rotated, the front one going round to the back

parts.note: 'did' as in 'I did the job' means finished it

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a cycling event at some point inside a calendar month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like the sport but rotates the letters, giving IDD; 'within' signals the insertion. The definition is the bare number 12, read as twelve o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock noon is the moment called midday.

clue.text: M&S stocks European rubbers

definitions.note: people who give rubs, a plural noun

indicators.note: a shop that stocks something holds it inside

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass, & is and, and S stays as it is
EUR is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Marks & Spencer, the British high-street store, sells European erasers.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S reads as the shop Marks & Spencer, but M is the physics symbol for mass; 'stocks' means contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Masseurs give massages, rubbing clients' muscles for a living.

clue.text: Organised cool and shady place where most children go

indicators.note: these letters are arranged in an orderly new way

explanation.surface: A well-planned, cool, shaded spot where most youngsters head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised cool and shady' rearranges the letters of COOL plus SHADY; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Most children attend a school by day rather than boarding.

clue.text: Like cooking naked

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, the word loses first and last letters

parts.note: baking is a way of cooking

explanation.surface: Something resembling cooking in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips BAKING of its outer letters B and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means similar, as in 'akin to', so it stands for like.

clue.text: Transferable skill acquired in the field?

definitions.meaning: ... describes an illness that passes from one person to another
... the ball is a fielding skill in cricket

explanation.surface: A careers-advice phrase about learning skills on the job that carry over to other work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transferable skill' reads as one CV phrase, but the clue splits after 'Transferable'. 'In the field' is cricket, where fielders take catches.
explanation.definitionFit: An infectious disease is called catching; snaring the ball in cricket is also catching.

clue.text: Said "Yes!" when journalist dispatched lines

indicators.note: to line something is to fill its inside, so the sent piece forms the lining of the outer one

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A reporter agreed as they filed copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like a reporter's copy, but it is the verb: one piece forms the lining of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree, so saying yes is assenting.

clue.text: Support available in 14 versions

indicators.note: the answer can be found within the following words

parts.note: 14 stands for the entry at 14-down, MERCANTILE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brace offered in fourteen models.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 refers to the answer at 14-down, MERCANTILE; the answer runs across MERCANTILE VERSIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam that supports a balcony or bridge.

clue.text: I failed audition leaving out dancing

definitions.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is India

indicators.note: a failed attempt goes wrong, so these letters are scrambled
the letters to be removed are jumbled too, not in their order

explanation.surface: A contestant moans about flopping in the audition, cut from the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: AUDITION, its letters jumbled ('failed'), loses the letters of OUT, scattered ('dancing'), leaving A D I I N. 'leaving' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: India is the radio code word for the letter I in the NATO alphabet.

clue.text: Place for person who made a killing backing substantial speculative venture?

definitions.text: Place for person who made a killing

indicators.note: going backwards, the word is reversed

parts.note: big means substantial
a bet is a wager, a speculative venture

explanation.surface: An investor who made a fortune is backing a big gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a killing' suggests a financial win, but means a murder: murderers were hanged and displayed on gibbets. 'backing' turns BIG into GIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet was a gallows where executed murderers were hanged.

clue.text: Hostile nation bombed Yemen

indicators.note: a bombed place is blown apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An unfriendly country carried out air raids on Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a hostile power or nation one is at war with.

clue.text: Gloomy spirit consuming adult faced by foul place

indicators.note: the piece after it stands in front of the rest

parts.note: a sty, where pigs live, is a byword for a filthy place

indicators.note: one piece eats, i.e. contains, the other

parts.note: gin is a spirit
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A dismal drinker's gin is downed by a grown-up in a squalid dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' gives GIAN; 'faced by' puts the foul place in front. Stygian comes from the Styx, the river of the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian, after the underworld river Styx, means very dark and dismal.

clue.text: Swimmer with smooth stroke

definitions.note: in crosswords a swimmer is often a fish

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth it
a dab is a light stroke or touch

explanation.surface: A swimmer with an easy, fluid swimming stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' and 'stroke' both suggest the pool, but the swimmer is a fish and the stroke a dab of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanddab is a small flatfish of the Pacific, so it swims.

clue.text: Make cuts and the rest start to heckle

parts.note: etc., short for et cetera, means and the rest

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone trims a speech, plus everything else, as a heckler begins to interrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave by cutting lines into a surface.

clue.text: Supply tape machine missing core component free

indicators.note: read as 'in a supple way', it tells us these letters bend into a new order
the word loses its central letter, its core

explanation.surface: An instruction to provide a cassette recorder that lacks a vital part, perhaps for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal. 'missing core component' drops H, the middle of MACHINE, leaving MACINE; TAPE plus MACINE rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate someone is to set them free, as slaves were liberated.

clue.text: Confused men with article related to commerce

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Muddled men with a newspaper piece about trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges MEN plus ARTICLE; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means having to do with merchants and trade.

clue.text: He revels in corruption engulfing current head of state

indicators.note: the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption
I is the physics symbol for electric current
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Britain's queen, the head of state

explanation.surface: A ruler's critic delights in the sleaze surrounding the present monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfing' gives RIOT. Elizabeth Regina's royal cipher is the usual crossword head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A rioter runs riot, and 'revel' in old usage means to riot in noisy merrymaking.

clue.text: Game in which one's rook always retreats

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: one's is read as 'I's', the Roman numeral I standing for one
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: In this board game a player's castle keeps falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' turns ISREVER back to front. Reversi, also sold as Othello, is a board game of flipping counters, so 'rook' teases chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversi is a two-player board game played with counters that flip colour.

clue.text: Close down high school admitting intelligence must take priority

indicators.note: the piece before comes first, ahead of the one named earlier
the school lets the next piece in

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness
meat that is high has gone off

explanation.surface: Shutting down a secondary school because cleverness must come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high school' reads as one phrase but splits: high is rotten, as food gone off. 'admitting' signals the insertion; 'must take priority' puts the school part first.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch off a machine is to shut it down.

clue.text: Confuse fish after casting net

indicators.note: the fishing piece comes after the scrambled one
casting, as with a net or a mould, throws the letters into a new shape

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: Fishermen tangle the line after throwing out a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' rearranges net into ENT; 'after' orders the pieces. 'fish' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle someone is to muddle or involve them in confusion.

clue.text: Trainee content to walk home

definitions.note: an adjective, as in home affairs

parts.note: an intern is a trainee, as in a hospital

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside letters

explanation.surface: A junior employee happy to stroll back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'satisfied' but means the inside of WALK. 'home' is the adjective, as in the Home Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal affairs are domestic, or home, matters, as opposed to foreign.

clue.text: Cutting support for members leads to industrial compensation board

indicators.note: the initials climb aboard, getting inside the sling

parts.note: a sling holds up an injured arm, a member or limb

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Reducing payments to injured workers via an industrial compensation board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a noun after 'compensation' but is the verb: the initials climb aboard. 'leads to' picks the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Slicing is cutting something into thin pieces.

clue.text: The French soldier applied to this

definitions.text: The French soldier applied to this

parts.note: le is French for the
GI is an American soldier
something applied to a surface is on it

explanation.surface: A French soldier enlisted in this outfit, the Foreign Legion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a French soldier might apply to join the Foreign Legion.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a body of soldiers, famously the French Foreign Legion.

clue.text: People left in charge after lead's assumed by United

indicators.note: the pieces before it follow the earlier one
the lead takes on, i.e. takes in, United

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
U is the abbreviation for United, as in team names

explanation.surface: Fans take charge when the team's top spot is taken by United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed by' gives PUB; 'after' orders the rest. Lead is the metal, not first place.
explanation.definitionFit: The public are people in general, as in 'open to the public'.

clue.text: Accused's location is belying indictment primarily

definitions.text: Accused's location is belying indictment primarily

indicators.note: first and foremost, so the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A defendant claims to have been elsewhere, contradicting the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an alibi is where the accused says they were, which belies the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defendant's claim to have been somewhere else at the time of a crime.

clue.text: University having sufficient means to host study is beyond question

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; 'is undeniable' swaps in

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second in as its guest

parts.note: a den is a private study
being able to afford something is having the means for it

explanation.surface: A well-funded university that can house a study centre is clearly a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to host' signals the insertion. 'University' is the short form uni here, not the usual single letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undeniable cannot be disputed, so it is beyond question.

clue.text: Opening for deluge to pour down

definitions.note: a verb, as in down a drink

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: when it pours, heavy rain falls

explanation.surface: A gap that lets the floodwater run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction for the water but is the verb: drain a glass, down it.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain a glass is to drink it all, to down it.

clue.text: Problem for many people tackled by Isaac Newton

indicators.note: the answer is grasped by these words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A puzzle for a crowd that the great scientist took on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackled by' tells us the answer is held within Isaac Newton, across the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne, spots on the skin, troubles a great many teenagers and adults.

clue.text: Doctor reduced small amount to relieve distress

definitions.note: noun phrase for money given; alms is used as a mass noun

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered in order
cut down by one of its last letters

explanation.surface: A GP cut a little dose to ease suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts SMALL to SMAL; 'Doctor', a verb, rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are charitable gifts of money or food to the poor.

clue.text: Putting on record containing a terrible racket

indicators.note: the first piece holds the rest

parts.note: a log is a written record
a din is a loud, unpleasant noise

explanation.surface: Playing a record that holds an awful noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' signals the insertion. 'Putting on' is the definition in the sense of loading cargo, not playing a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Loading a lorry is putting goods on it.

clue.text: Express disapproval about every new increase in a dramatic manner

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, i.e. around, the second

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
all means every one

explanation.surface: Audiences jeer at each new swelling of the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the insertion. 'in a dramatic manner' belongs to the definition, not to theatre jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs that balloon swell rapidly, like a balloon being blown up.

clue.text: Bore detective with case of conservative member's complaint?

indicators.note: the detective is put inside a case made of the other pieces

parts.note: VD, venereal disease, is cheekily an affliction of the male member
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A dreary detective investigates a Tory MP's grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with case of' signals the wrap. The 'member' looks like a Member of Parliament, but is the bawdy sense; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, to carry, and conveyed means carried.

clue.text: Productive exercise almost complete

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: full means complete, as in a full set

explanation.surface: A worthwhile workout that is nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful serves a purpose, so it is productive.
